name: KVQuant (per-channel + pre-RoPE key quantization, non-uniform KV)
bits: 3-bit keys and values are the headline (<0.1 perplexity degradation); the method is a toolkit that also supports 2-bit and 4-bit
activation_scheme: Not an activation scheme - KV cache. Four components: (i) per-channel key quantization; (ii) PRE-RoPE key quantization - keys are quantized BEFORE the rotary positional embedding is applied, mitigating the way RoPE smears quantization error across the rotation; (iii) non-uniform per-layer sensitivity-weighted datatypes; (iv) per-vector dense-and-sparse quantization isolating outliers separately for each vector.
kernels: Custom CUDA kernels developed for KVQuant; the paper reports throughput results with them but the abstract truncates the figure.
quality_delta: From the abstract: '<0.1 perplexity degradation with 3-bit quantization on both Wikitext-2 and C4', outperforming existing approaches, across LLaMA, Llama-2, Llama-3 and Mistral. Enables serving LLaMA-7B at up to 1 million context on a single A100-80GB and up to 10 million on an 8-GPU system.
notes:
GROUP SIZE NOT APPLICABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: this scheme quantizes the KV cache, not the weights, so there are no weight groups to size. A number in this field would be a category error. (Where the underlying method has a real grouping - e.g. KIVI per-channel keys, KVQuant per-channel - that lives in the method's own record, not in weight_group_size.) Second KV record; same enum mismatch as KIVI (no KV-cache enum exists). The substantive addition here is PRE-RoPE KEY QUANTIZATION, which is the single most transferable idea in the KV-quantization literature: RoPE rotates the key vector, and a rotation applied AFTER quantization mixes each coordinate with several others, so the quantization error is no longer axis-aligned and cannot be corrected per-channel. Quantizing first and rotating second keeps the error structured. This matters for the rotation family too - QuaRot and SpinQuant rotate the KV cache as well, and doing that BEFORE quantization is what makes it work. Dense-and-sparse per-vector outlier handling here is the same trick as LLM.int8(), Atom and SqueezeLLM, now applied to the cache. The 10-million-token claim is a memory-capacity claim enabled by 3-bit KV, not a latency claim. SCHEME RECLASSIFIED (parent agent, 2026-10-03): scheme was 'bitsandbytes-nf4' (a proxy recorded while the enum lacked a legal value) and is now 'kv-cache-quant'. 
NATIVE_SUPPORT CLASSIFIED 2026-10-04: this field is still [] and that is CORRECT, but the empty list used to be ambiguous between three different states and now is not. Reason class on this record: KV-CACHE-ONLY, SO STRUCTURALLY ABSENT. The bits field records that no bits-per-value change: the scheme reduces WHICH positions are retained, fetched or reallocated, so it runs on whatever precision path the accelerator already has for the KV cache. A KV-position policy can never be a hardware format. Consequence for a reader: nothing further to verify - this is a cache-management policy, not a numeric format. The full statement of the three-way distinction, and the worked list of all 72 empty records by class, is in gotcha quant-native-support-empty-means-three-different-things. Rule of thumb for this field everywhere in the repo: if the bits field carries an 'a16', or the scheme is KV-cache-only or a llama.cpp integer storage type, an empty native_support is a DEFINITION and needs no verification; only a W4A4/W8A8/sub-8-bit format with research kernels can have an empty list that is a real finding.
